thread:
monitoring-bot: ALERT hosted-inference-gateway: sustained 5xx spike in us-west-2 (3.1k errors / 5m). SLO breach potential. paging #oncall
alex: I'm oncall — jumping in. Any customer-facing outages reported?
dana: Support: a handful of customers reported repeated timeouts 30m ago, putting in a ticket for customer A (cust-479).
ben: grabbing traces now. initial look: increased 502s from gateway -> runtime vms during kv-cache window changes.
cara: seeing backlog on gateway queues + long tail in service-time histograms around token generation step.
alex: mitigation idea: enable gateway circuit-breaker to fail fast and route to fallback model variant. @ben can you validate fallback compatibility?
ben: fallback variant exists (llama-7b-quant) — quality lower but stable. I can flip route at the gateway layer.
dana: coordinate comms if we flip for affected customers. Ellen on support thread — keep them updated.
alex: do we have a quick repro? need to reproduce locally to confirm root cause.
ben: repro steps I'm using:
```
# quick reproducer (from customer request)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gptx-peak","input":"repeat:\n"}' --max-time 30 -v
```
ben: with a loop of parallel requests (20 concurrent) I can trigger 502 after ~90s. stack traces show kv-cache stall + oom-ish schedule delays.
cara: looks like host-level GC / GPU kernel stalls. I'm checking node telemetry (nvml, IO wait).
ben: logs snippet: 
```
[2026-03-16T10:12:23Z] runtime: kv_cache: stall detected, waiting for lock 120s
[2026-03-16T10:12:24Z] gateway: upstream read timeout, code=502
[2026-03-16T10:14:01Z] runtime: worker exit: SIGBUS? stack: ...
```
alex: ok, immediate mitigations: 1) enable gateway circuit-breaker for suspect routes (fail fast), 2) scale runtime pool + drain suspect hosts, 3) enable fallback to quant-variant for affected endpoints. Which one should we do first?
cara: flip circuit-breaker first (no customer change), then fallback route for high-traffic customers to reduce pressure. scaling will be background and may take 5-10m.
dana: I'll update customer A and the support queue: letting them know we are failing fast to reduce errors and routing to fallback if needed.
ben: performing circuit-breaker flip now: `deploy-bot: starting rollout of cb-policy v2 -> gateway`
deploy-bot: cb-policy v2 rollout started (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%). monitors: https://telemetry.redwood.ai/d/gateway/errors?org=prod
alex: monitoring dashboard — error rate already trending down on canary. good sign.
cara: kicked off a scale up for runtime pool in us-west-2: `kubectl scale deployment/runtime-pool --replicas=20 -n hosted` (scaling from 12 -> 20).
ben: enabling fallback route for top 5 affected routes now.
dana: comms: posted to customer A: "We are failing fast and routing to a stable fallback model while we investigate root cause. No data loss. Will follow up."
ellen: customer A response: appreciative, asking for ETA on permanent fix.
ben: still seeing occasional 502s from a small subset of hosts; I'm isolating host IDs and draining them from LB. host ids: i-0a1b2c3d, i-0f2e3d4c
cara: draining hosts now and tossing kernel logs to infra for analysis.
ben: repro reduced when kv-cache prefetch disabled (quick toggled in runtime config). pushing small config canary to 5% first.
alex: good. Can we get short-term action items and an owner for postmortem?
cara: action items (short):
- bisect runtime change that introduced kv-cache lock (ben)
- review GPU driver/kernel combo on drained hosts (cara + eng-infra)
- add circuit-breaker default to degrade earlier for high-queue-length routes (alex + eng-platform)
- improve observability: surface kv-cache lock metrics and per-host OOM/stack traces (ben)
- customer follow-up: Dana to own comms and timeline
ben: owning bisect (eta 48h). I'll post PR references in the follow-up thread.
cara: infra for kernel/driver check (eta 24h).
dana: I'll draft post-incident note for customers and internal stakeholders.
alex: let's schedule a 30m sync in 2 hours to review logs and next steps.
ben: saving repro artifacts here: https://storage.redwood.ai/incidents/3571234567/repro.tar.gz
cara: creating postmortem doc stub and owner fields: assigned to alex for sign-off.
deploy-bot: circuit-breaker rollout complete to 100% (timestamp 2026-03-16T10:22:30Z).
alex: last check — error rate down to baseline, backlog cleared. moving to recovery state.
dana: support: closing urgent ticket for customer A, will leave follow-up for latest ETA.
alex: closing war room. postmortem owners and action items above. please add any missing notes here. 
ben: note: add automated smoke test that runs parallel requests at low qps to catch kv-cache regressions in canary pipeline.
cara: also recommend a small runtime config guard: reject requests beyond X tokens when queue depth > Y.
dana: I'll add a bullet for customer comms timeline in the postmortem doc.
alex: thanks team. Blameless postmortem, action owners assigned.
monitoring-bot: INCIDENT: severity downgraded to P2, incident closed by alex at 2026-03-16T10:56:07Z
